A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModernNCA work despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable. v2 intentionally replaces some detailed tables with external references; this is a reporting change, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and regression experiments on 22 datasets, ablations, runtime measurements, and appendix results with standard deviations.

after.justification: v2 reports original comparisons across 300 datasets, component analyses on a 45-dataset benchmark, statistical comparisons, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: The final ModernNCA pipeline retains PLR-lite and categorical encoding, the embedding architecture, classification log loss and regression MSE, Euclidean neighbor weighting, training-time neighborhood sampling, and full-training-set inference. v1 already includes a linear variant; v2's L-NCA-to-M-NCA presentation expands the explanation and component analysis without establishing a revised final algorithm.

E1.justification: The main evaluation expands from 8 binary classification, 4 multiclass classification, and 10 regression datasets to a reported 120, 80, and 100 datasets respectively. Ablations use a 45-dataset benchmark instead of four selected datasets. The temporal-shift and high-dimensional limitations discussion does not establish additional evaluations by this work.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 substantially expands the comparison set, adding methods including SVM, RandomForest, LightGBM, SAINT, SwitchTab, and ExcelFormer. LMNN and TabCon leave the principal benchmark comparison; original NCA appears in component analyses, while TabCon retains appendix discussion and visualization. TabR also joins the PLR ablation, unlike v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: v2 adds staged NCA controls and a fixed two-layer MLP experiment that tunes only architecture-independent hyperparameters. It removes the few-shot subsampling protocol and changes resource reporting from checkpoint size in MB to memory usage in GB, without specifying the latter's measurement procedure. The main split, accuracy/RMSE metrics, batch size, and 100-trial search remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds sequential tests of projection dimension, optimizer, loss, and inference; comparisons with MCML and t-distribution losses; and fixed-architecture controls. Retained architecture, encoding, distance, and sampling analyses gain broader evidence. v1's few-shot study and TabCon KNN-versus-regression-predictor comparison disappear. The embedding visualization is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 15 seeds for the main evaluation. v2 adds t-test-based Win/Tie/Lose decisions at 95% confidence and Wilcoxon-Holm comparisons at significance level 0.05. Conversely, v1's per-dataset standard-deviation tables are absent from v2. This substantially changes statistical reporting without documenting an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–2 place ModernNCA first overall for both tasks; v2 Figure 2 places it first for classification and behind CatBoost for regression on the expanded benchmark. New Win/Tie/Lose ratios include 0.41/0.36/0.23 against TabR and 0.38/0.27/0.35 against CatBoost. Numerous ablation results are added or replaced. These concern different benchmark/comparator coverage, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The probability formulas revise the normalization exclusion from the candidate neighbor in v1 Equations 3–4 to the query instance in v2 Equations 2–4. Appendix B.2 also expresses the inner-product distance using mapped features instead of raw inputs. These are limited mathematical-formulation corrections; neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds a central claim that improved linear NCA can compete with MLPs and reframes the contribution around systematic component analysis. Its abstract narrows v1's broad superiority over tree-based models to performance on par with CatBoost, with the introduction explicitly acknowledging second place in regression.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving optimization benefits from higher-dimensional linear projections and PLR compensating for architectural simplicity. New Appendix B.5 identifies temporal relationships and high-dimensional data as limitations and discusses mitigations. Some interpretation is overstated: the claim that PLR improves all methods conflicts with Table 4, where TabR's regression rank worsens from 3.167 to 3.444.

D1.justification: v1's dataset metadata table and detailed TabCon instructions for normalization, quantile binning, and predictor validation disappear. v2 delegates dataset and implementation details to other papers and supplies a specific external results-directory pointer. It adds optimizer and PLR-lite weight-sharing explanations. The original code repository, V100 hardware disclosure, and principal training settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated NCA-variants discussion and explicitly acknowledges earlier neural NCA extensions by Salakhutdinov and Hinton and by Min et al., positioning this work as their modern revisit. New baseline, benchmarking, soft-neighbor-loss, and limitations references substantially broaden the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the title changes, and the method becomes a two-stage narrative. Analyses receive a separate main section, related work is reorganized around NCA variants, and TabCon material moves into a shortened appendix treatment. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: Dataset-level result tables give way to Win/Tie/Lose summaries and critical-difference diagrams. Sampling curves become aggregate-rank bars, several ablations become redesigned aggregate tables, and new component/loss/control tables appear. Few-shot plots and full uncertainty tables disappear. Figure 1 is redrawn, while the embedding visualization is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The broader evaluations, statistical comparisons, and staged and fixed-architecture ablations substantially strengthen v1's limited evidence for generality and individual design choices. More accurate prior-work positioning, qualified CatBoost comparisons, and explicit limitations improve scientific interpretation. Removing dataset metadata and standard-deviation tables reduces self-contained reproducibility, and the PLR discussion contains an overstatement, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and qualification.
